Java XXE hardening was stated as one uniform recipe across DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory and TransformerFactory; the four do not share an API and two throw when it is applied. Split into per-factory lines: setExpandEntityReferences is DBF-only, StAX uses setProperty SUPPORT_DTD / IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, TransformerFactory uses ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD / ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET and does not recognise disallow-doctype-decl

Three owned slugs had no severity row. Added five rows: whole-model serialization returning authentication material (authz-property-level); proxy path-prefix ACL the application does not enforce, and caller-supplied forwarding header trusted for a decision (request-smuggling-and-proxy-normalization); identifier in a URL, and request logger writing credentials or whole bodies (application-log-and-url-content). The identifier-in-URL row is the base grade hipaa-and-phi and privacy-and-data-protection uplift from, and its absence broke both inbound deferrals

Deleted the unfalsifiable "or the path terminates at an edge the repository does not contain" clause from the rate-limit re-graded row. The only exemption is now delegated authentication, established from an OIDC/SAML client and no password comparison in any handler. Reconciled the row rationale, the severity row and false positive 5 to that same condition
a six-digit code with no limit is a ten-thousand-request problem was arithmetically wrong; 10^6 is a million and ten thousand is a four-digit code

A mutating GET is not forgeable by an img tag "regardless of SameSite"; Lax cookies are withheld from cross-site subresource requests. The carriers are top-level navigations - window.location, window.open, a link, a 302

Credentialed CORS reflection was listed as a CSRF delivery path in three places (item 9, the re-graded table, false positive 1). It is a response-read defect and does not cause a Lax cookie to be attached. Corrected in all three, with its real CSRF role - reading the anti-CSRF token out of a response - stated once

The safeHref nomatch accepted a backslash-form protocol-relative URL, the bypass item 12 names as most-missed. Replaced the startsWith pair with a regex requiring one leading slash followed by neither slash nor backslash

The NoSQL detector's explanation claimed a $ne-on-password payload authenticates against its own match sample, where hash() coerces the password before the query. Rewritten: username is the injectable field there and the attack is a username-free password spray. R5 now probes both fields

production and unrotated cannot be established from a repository, so the browser-bundle Critical could never fire. Re-conditioned on a live-environment prefix or shape plus presence at HEAD; rotation is recorded as a client question, not a grade input

frameworks declares cwe and the body claimed identifiers are cited inline, with zero CWE identifiers in the file. Frontmatter is out of scope this round, so the claim was made true rather than withdrawn: a nine-row item-to-CWE table, with CWE-208 routed to crypto

Angular innerHTML binding is sanitized through DomSanitizer by default and is not an escaping opt-out; listing it produced a false positive against idiomatic Angular. The opt-out is the bypassSecurityTrust family. Also scoped data:text/html and vbscript: as illustrations rather than live paths
costLimitPlugin and maxDepthPlugin are not exported from the graphql-armor aggregate package, which exports ApolloArmor; the nomatch import would not resolve. Switched to the per-rule packages

ImageMagick does not implement the GNU end-of-options convention, so passing it to convert makes it a filename operand. Removed from the nomatch and replaced with a server-generated path; added a rule that the convention is tool-specific and must be checked before being recommended

A parameterised SET LOCAL works only on drivers that interpolate client-side and fails on psycopg3 and asyncpg. Changed the RLS nomatch to set_config, and taught both the prose and the cross-tenant severity row to search for both spellings so a set_config codebase is not read as having no RLS

Rails order and pluck over caller-supplied columns were stated flatly; Rails 6+ raises UnknownAttributeReference unless the value is wrapped in Arel.sql, so on a supported Rails the finding is the wrapper

Express query-string object coercion was stated as version-independent; Express 5 changed the default query parser. Re-anchored the rule on req.body under express.json(), which holds on every version, with the query-string path marked version-conditional

The unsafe-yaml-load and BinaryFormatter sinks were stated flatly. PyYAML 6 made the Loader argument mandatory and FullLoader is not RCE; BinaryFormatter is obsoleted and disabled by default in recent .NET and remains correct only as a legacy sink

Apollo Server 4 defaults - introspection off under production, batched HTTP requests off, CSRF prevention shipped - carry three grades and are library defaults that move between majors. Scoped to Apollo Server 4 explicitly, with an instruction to read the major from the lockfile

The A09:2025 category title could not be re-verified from this session and was left unchanged rather than guessed at in either direction. Recorded the provenance of the lock and an instruction to re-verify against owasp.org before publication, with the blast radius named

The deserialization Critical row still read "yaml.load without a safe loader" and listed BinaryFormatter flatly, contradicting the corrected item-16 prose and producing a false Critical on yaml.load(data, Loader=yaml.FullLoader) and on any BinaryFormatter reference in a modern .NET project. Row now splits unconditional sinks from the two version-conditional ones: yaml.load earns it only with Loader=yaml.Loader or UnsafeLoader (FullLoader excluded by name, safe_load named as the fix, PyYAML 6 mandatory-Loader stated), and BinaryFormatter earns it on .NET Framework or from a quotable re-enabling artifact - the EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization MSBuild property or AppContext switch, plus the System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters compatibility package on .NET 9+ where the in-box implementation always throws. Switch names and the .NET 9 removal verified verbatim against learn.microsoft.com binaryformatter-migration-guide and its compatibility-package page

The nomatch presented an Apollo Server 4 construction whose plugins array held maxDepthPlugin and costLimitPlugin from the per-rule packages. Those exports are Envelop plugins, not ApolloServerPlugin objects, so the sample marketed as safe applied no depth or cost limit at all. Rewritten to the documented Apollo integration: new ApolloArmor({ maxDepth: { n: 8 }, costLimit: { maxCost: 5000 } }), protect() spread into the constructor with both returned arrays re-spread. Verified against packages/graphql-armor/src/apollo/armor.ts and src/apollo/protections/{max-depth,cost-limit}.ts on the Escape-Technologies/graphql-armor main branch - protect() returns plugins, validationRules, allowBatchedHttpRequests false and includeStacktraceInErrorResponses false, and both limits are mounted as validation rules built from maxDepthRule and costLimitRule - and against escape.tech/graphql-armor/docs/getting-started, which shows the same spread form; config key names maxDepth and costLimit read off GraphQLArmorConfig in packages/types/src/index.ts

Consumer sweep of the same claim: the depth-and-complexity bullet named graphql-depth-limit, graphql-query-complexity and graphql-armor as controls without saying where each mounts, which is what let the broken nomatch look plausible. The bullet now states the rule once at the point of statement - read the mounting slot, not the import; on Apollo Server 4 depth and cost are validation rules, while the per-rule graphql-armor exports are Envelop plugins that never run in Apollo plugins array

Second consumer of the same claim, wrong in both directions and not named in the re-review: the missing depth-or-complexity row cleared on the presence of a plugin. As written it cleared a mis-wired Envelop plugin sitting in Apollo plugins array (a false all-clear on an unprotected server) and filed a High against a correctly armored Apollo server that carries the limits in validationRules and nothing in plugins (a false High). Row now grades on the control being mounted in a slot the engine executes, names both outcomes explicitly, and refers the ambiguous case to R7 resolver spies
